title: Three Swift dip brackets require 1.10-day timing shifts under fixed 30-percent levels and the published ASASSN-14ko decay
abstract: We test the ASASSN-14ko X-ray clock without a dip template or a time probability law inside visit gaps. We build exact sets of possible downward-crossing intervals from a verified Swift and NICER visit table. At fixed 30-percent suppression and one reported rate-error unit, three Swift cycles require a delay range of at least 2.2097 days under the published local decay. The smallest possible maximum absolute timing shift is 1.1049 days; the full nine-cycle fit attains this algebraic bound. A constant clock is allowed. Independent suppression levels from 20 to 60 percent reduce the required shift to 0.5265 days. With two rate-error units, that variable-level model permits the published decay with zero shift. The result gives a sharp conditional bound and a limit on a stronger inference from sampling alone. The feasible sets are not confidence intervals. The test assumes an event within each search window and a sampled high-to-low transition. It does not identify pericentre, model correlated noise, or fit XMM and Einstein Probe data. Code, exact interval sets and clock witnesses permit reproduction.

display.caption: Exact crossing sets and feasible clock curvature under fixed and variable suppression levels. Ranges are deterministic, not confidence intervals.
